set.approach: Hike past The Gardens, then follow a trail up the steep, rocky hillside, splitting left or right depending on which formation you want. Deviled Egg is on the right side of the Egg's north face, a large rounded block with a downed tree at its base, uphill and a little northwest of the Lime-Aid formation.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no counts stated.

set.approach: Park near the County Road 805 gate without blocking the road. Walk past the old cabin, follow the path beside the small creek, then climb a talus field; turn left at the creek sign and keep going up to the mine tailings, which mark the base of the cliff. Talus and tailings are loose, so wear sturdy shoes.
set.descent_text: The four bolted routes have fixed anchors for top-roping or leading; parties downclimb or rappel from them. Check the hardware before trusting it.

From the ranch approach, hike south to the cliffs; alternatively, take a short walk east from the Forest Service road. The way is a moderate hike through forest patches and across granite slabs and open faces.

set.approach: Park in the big grassy meadow along East Fork Road above US 160. The south-facing crag can be seen from the parking area; the approach is a short, steep scramble up below it. The rock is loose.

set.approach: Park in the Stairway to Heaven lot off County Road 2 toward Eureka. The buttress is on the west side of the road directly across from the lot, a short walk straight up a scree field. set.approach: Two ways lead to the north face. From the Priest Lake side, the Chimney trail leads to Roothaan, and the ridge from there descends to Gunsight. From Hunt Lake, which is significantly shorter, go around the back left side of Gunsight and traverse in below the north face. The route climbs the middle of the face.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no counts stated.

set.approach: Park as for the Lion Creek water slides and go through the concrete barricades. Follow cairns and rough paths down to the creek crossing, then hike up and left through boulders and scree, past a few cairns, to the base of the slabs.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no counts stated.

set.approach: Park in the pullouts just outside The Gap on the east side and continue up Arimo Road several hundred meters. The climbs are on the south side of the road, and a small creek crossing is needed to reach them.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no counts stated.

set.approach: From the Wolverine trailhead, stay left up a pair of switchbacks to an old fire road and follow it to a Forest Service trail sign pointing right. That trail runs to the largest meadow, where it meets a creek you do not cross; take the beaten path across the meadow to the cairn on the rise before the trees, then keep to the well-worn trail up to the big meadow below the bowl. The climbers' trail crosses that meadow straight to the base of Lower Replica. From there, follow the trail up and right alongside the cliff to the scree field between Lower and Upper Replica, cross it, pass below Upper Replica to a second short scree field, and continue up and left. The first route you reach is Boy Scout Hand Grenade; the rest sit on a small treed ledge a bit farther up the slope.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no counts stated.

set.approach: Park at the bridge over Emigrant Creek and walk up the road, or drive a high-clearance 4x4 farther until the buttresses show up and to the right. The approach is undeveloped, steep scree that can be loose and slippery.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no counts stated.

set.approach: Begin at the lot for the Old Man historic site and hike the Greenleaf Trail uphill toward the AMC Greenleaf Hut. Where the trail levels off shortly before Eagle Pass, a small cairn on the left marks the start of the climbers' trail. Bear left at each fork, stay in the trees on the left and keep out of the talus field on the right; if the climbers' trail goes on much longer than expected, you missed a fork. The Main Wall faces southwest and gets sun all day.

review.notes: Crag-level approach from the area page(s); no counts stated.

set.approach: From the hairpin corner in an aspen grove on Hinkey Summit Road, where there is room to park or a small pullout just back down the road, a faint-to-defined trail leads east toward the wall. It crosses two drainages before reaching the base. The Cleft is the prominent west-facing slab, split by a vertical gully into a north wall and a south wall.
